seed: A window too short to hold two open effects at once, which is where the Effects list has to choose which of them to keep room for. The rule it follows is the same one the rest of the panel follows: what you just did is what you can see. So the room goes to the effect you just ADDED, and then to the effect you just OPENED, and the other one is the one that runs past the cut. Every press is followed by a reading of the chevron it aimed at, so a press that lands on nothing fails on the spot rather than quietly leaving the walk a fold out of step.

steps.comment: A window too short to hold two open effects at once.
A fresh box comes with its outline already in the list, open. That is the effect the room starts with.
Add a second effect. Its settings used to arrive below the bottom edge of the list, with nothing scrolling to them: you had added a shadow and there was nothing on it to set.

steps.note: the Shadow is the effect you just added, so it is the one the list keeps room for: the whole pane, with the Border's tail showing through the fade above it

steps.comment: Now fold the one above it away. Folding is not a command about a thing that appeared, so nothing is revealed for it.
Open it again: the room moves to it, and the Shadow becomes the one that runs past the cut.
A full second, not half of one: opening a pane lengthens the list under the scroller, which slides every heading below it.

steps.note: the Border is the effect being worked on now, so the Effects list is back to the room the Border needs

steps.comment: And once more from the bottom: open the LOWER effect by hand. This used to show its top half only, because the room went to the first open effect in the list rather than to the one just pressed.

steps.note: the room moves back down to the Shadow, and the Border's tail is what shows through the fade above it
